name: Chole Bhature
description: Thick spiced chickpea gravy with bhatura, a deep-fried bread of white flour, sometimes stuffed with potato or paneer. It is one of Chandigarh's most popular meals.
how_to_eat: Eat it with green chutney, onion and pickle, and a lassi on the side.
how_to_order: Ask for a plate of 'chole bhature' at sector market eateries.

name: Amritsari Kulcha
description: Tandoor-baked flatbread stuffed with potato, paneer, onion or gobhi, topped with butter. Roadside stalls across the city sell it.
how_to_eat: Eat it with spicy chole, chutney and pickle.
how_to_order: Ask for an 'aloo' or 'mix kulcha' with chole at kulcha stalls, such as those in Sector 9.

name: Rajma Chawal
description: Red kidney beans in a thick spicy tomato-onion gravy, served with jeera or steamed rice. It is a filling, everyday favourite in the city.
how_to_eat: Mix the rajma into the rice and add onion and pickle.
how_to_order: Ask for a plate of 'rajma chawal' at small eateries in sector markets.

name: Chicken Tikka
description: Chicken marinated in curd, turmeric, cumin, ginger-garlic and chilli, skewered and grilled over charcoal. It is a signature dish of the city.
how_to_eat: Eat it with lime, chutney and onion rings.
how_to_order: Ask for a half or full plate of 'chicken tikka' at tikka stalls and dhabas.

name: Sarson da Saag with Makki di Roti
description: Mashed mustard greens with spices, eaten with flat cornbread and plenty of butter and ghee. The Punjabi classic is served from street stalls to fine dining in Chandigarh.
how_to_eat: Top it with white butter and eat with the makki roti.
how_to_order: Ask for 'saag makki' in winter at dhabas.

name: Butter Chicken
description: Grilled chicken pieces in a buttery, smooth tomato and onion gravy. It is a staple at Chandigarh's non-vegetarian restaurants.
how_to_order: Ask for half or full 'butter chicken' at dhabas.

name: Paneer Tikka
description: Paneer cubes grilled on skewers with peppers and onions. It is a North Indian street food favourite in the city.
how_to_eat: Eat it with lime and green chutney.
how_to_order: Ask for a plate of 'paneer tikka' at tikka stalls.

name: Lassi
description: A chilled yogurt drink, sweet or salted, sometimes with dry fruits. Locals often follow a meal with lassi or buttermilk.
how_to_eat: Drink it cold after a heavy meal.
how_to_order: Ask for 'meethi' or 'namkeen lassi' at sweet shops such as those in Sector 17.

name: Gol Gappe
description: Crisp hollow puris filled with potato and chickpeas and dipped in spicy or sweet flavoured water. Chaat stalls in Sector 23 have served them since the 1960s.
how_to_eat: Eat each one in one bite.
how_to_order: Stand at a chaat stall and ask for a plate of 'gol gappe'.

name: Tikki Chaat
description: Crisp potato patties topped with chickpeas, yogurt and chutneys. It is a famous order at the city's long-running chaat stalls.
how_to_eat: Eat it hot from the plate with a spoon.
how_to_order: Ask for 'tikki chaat' at chaat stalls in sector markets.

name: Dahi Bhalla
description: Fried lentil fritters soaked and served in yogurt with chutneys and spices. Sector 11's market stalls sell it with other chaat.
how_to_eat: Eat it cold with a spoon.
how_to_order: Ask for a plate of 'dahi bhalla' at chaat stalls.
